subject.title: [Feature]: Non-interactive command to use Codex OAuth for model provider

question: Should OpenClaw add a non-interactive OpenAI/Codex OAuth setup surface, and which secret-bearing callback/code/session contract is acceptable?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but the proposed environment-variable callback URL changes the auth-provider security boundary and may conflict with the current explicit OAuth posture.

options.title: Design a safer import contract
options.body: Prefer a plugin-owned command or setup surface that ingests callback/code/session material through a leak-resistant channel and preserves PKCE/state validation before persisting auth.

options.title: Accept callback URL env import
options.body: Allow the requested env-var style only if maintainers explicitly accept the leakage risk and require strict redaction, validation, and documentation.

options.title: Defer non-interactive OAuth
options.body: Keep browser, remote paste, device-code, and API-key login as the supported paths until upstream Codex exposes a stable external auth handoff.

recommendation.title: Design a safer import contract
recommendation.body: Prefer a plugin-owned command or setup surface that ingests callback/code/session material through a leak-resistant channel and preserves PKCE/state validation before persisting auth.
